nodes.name: Polyol synthesis of HENPs
nodes.procedure: Eight different metal precursors AlCl₃ (anhydrous), SnCl₂·2H₂O, CoCl₂·6H₂O, NiCl₂·6H₂O, CuCl₂ (anhydrous), IrCl₃·xH₂O, CeCl₃·7H₂O, and RhCl₃·xH₂O were dissolved in 50 ml deionized (DI) water. Separately, 0.55 mg of poly(N-vinyl-2-pyrrolidone) (PVP) and 0.2 g of NaBH₄ were dissolved in 150 mL of triethylene glycol (TEG). The metals precursor solution was added dropwise into the preheated TEG solution at 230°C under stirring for 2 h, then allowed to cool. The octonary AlSnCoNiCuIrCeRh HENPs were separated via centrifugation with acetone and washed with ethanol and DI water several times to remove excess PVP. The resultant black powder was dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C. To construct the dataset for exploring the optimal composition, molar concentrations of the metal precursors were randomly selected, as detailed in Table S1 (Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals ultra-small HENPs with mean size ≈2.02 nm (HER-optimized) and 1.85 nm (OER-optimized), uniformly distributed without aggregation, lattice fringes of 0.22 nm (111) and 0.19 nm (200) FCC facets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The particle size and microstructure of the HENPs were characterized using high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) (Figure 6a-c). A statistical analysis of fifty randomly selected nanoparticles indicated a mean size of ≈2.02 nm... These nanoparticles exhibited a particle size of 1.85 nm (Figure S18a, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns exhibit diffraction rings with discrete spots indexed to (111), (200), and (220) planes, confirming FCC crystallinity of the nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Selected area diffraction pattern (SAED) patterns (Figure 6c) exhibited diffraction rings with discrete spots, confirming the crystallinity of the nanoparticles, and the diffraction rings were indexed to the (111), (200), and (220) planes of the FCC structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD shows broad diffraction peaks at 40.9°, 52.98°, and 69.15° corresponding to (111), (200), and (220) planes of FCC-structured HENPs, with no distinct metallic peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern (Figure 6d) further corroborated the TEM findings, displaying broad diffraction peaks at 40.9°, 52.98°, and 69.15°, corresponding to the (111), (200), and (220) planes of FCC-structured HENPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping and line scanning reveal uniform distribution of all constituent elements (Al, Sn, Co, Ni, Cu, Ir, Ce, Rh) throughout the nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) mapping and line scanning profiles (Figure 6e-n; Figure S14, Supporting Information) revealed a uniform distribution of all constituent elements throughout the nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show characteristic peak at 561 cm⁻¹ attributed to M-O stretching vibration of high-entropy oxide (HEO) nanoparticles, with no individual metal oxide peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Figure S15, Supporting Information) showed a characteristic peak at 561 cm⁻¹, attributed to the M-O stretching vibration of high-entropy oxide (HEO) nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Al, Sn, Co, Ni, Cu, Ir, Ce, Rh, O with mixed oxidation states: strong oxidation peaks for Ce, Al, Sn (Al³⁺, Sn⁴⁺, Ce⁴⁺) and metallic peaks for Ir, Rh, Co, Ni, Cu, confirming HEA-HEO heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was employed to investigate the surface chemical states of the HENPs's elements. A survey scan spectrum confirmed the presence of Al, Sn, Co, Ni, Cu, Ir, Ce, Rh, and O (Figure S16, Supporting Information).
